# 多伦多找室友全攻略（2026版）

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-10-31

多伦多找室友怎么找才靠谱？本文从渠道选择、身份和房源核实、常见危险信号，一路讲到第一次见面要问什么、怎么签室友协议，留学生和新移民一篇就能看懂。

多伦多找室友，最稳妥的做法是：先想清楚预算和底线，再同时用两三个渠道找人；挑出生活习惯合拍的候选人，视频加当面聊过，核实对方身份和房源真实性；最后把规则写成室友协议，再付钱、再搬家。

听起来简单，但每一步都有坑。下面按顺序讲清楚，特别照顾第一次在加拿大租房的留学生和新移民。

## 先看要点

- **早点开始**：至少提前四到六周，开学季（八九月）要更早。
- **习惯比预算更重要**：作息、卫生、带朋友回家，才是室友矛盾的主要来源。
- **先核实，再付钱**：确认人是真的、房是真的、对方真的有权出租。
- **搞清楚自己的身份**：你是租约上的共同租客，还是"二房东"的室友，还是和业主同住？法律保护不一样。
- **写下来**：一两页的室友协议，能避免大多数纠纷。

## 第一步：想清楚自己要什么

在刷房源之前，先把这几件事写在手机备忘录里，后面每一次沟通都会快很多：

- **预算**：房租上限，加上你要分摊的水电、暖气和网费。多伦多单间租金因区域、房型、是否独立卫浴、是否包家具差别很大，网上看到的数字只能当粗略参考，最好多看几套同区域的房源自己对比。
- **位置**：离学校或公司多远？离地铁站、公交线近不近？冬天走路十五分钟和夏天走路十五分钟，体感完全不同。
- **入住时间和租期**：4个月、8个月还是一年？能不能灵活？很多留学生只需要一个学期，要提前和对方说清楚。
- **必须有的**：独立卫生间、室内洗衣机、停车位、可以养宠物、可以做中餐（油烟大不大是很多合租家庭真实会吵的点）。
- **绝对不能接受的**：抽烟、伴侣天天留宿、养狗、对方上夜班等。

### 合租形式有哪几种？

| 形式 | 含义 | 需要注意 |
|---|---|---|
| 共同租客 (co-tenants) | 所有人都在租约上签字 | 通常每个人都要对房东负责全部房租 |
| 租客的室友 | 只有一人签租约，你把钱交给他 | 你对房东的权利可能很有限，务必签室友协议 |
| 和业主同住 | 业主自己也住在房子里 | 如果和业主或其近亲共用厨房或卫生间，《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 可能不适用 |
| 整栋按房间分租 | 每人各租一间，同住一栋 | 问清楚公共费用和屋规怎么定 |

很多同学在微信群里租的"单间"，其实是第二种：一个人和房东签了约，再把其他房间转租出去，俗称"二房东"。这种情况下，你的押金交给谁、出了问题找谁，一定要事先问清楚。如果不确定自己属于哪一种，签约前可以咨询房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 或社区法律诊所。

## 第二步：多伦多找室友去哪里找？

不要只盯一个渠道，各有优缺点：

- **室友匹配平台**：可以先按预算、区域、生活习惯筛选，再开始聊，节省大量时间。比如在 ColivEase 上，AI 会根据作息、预算和生活习惯推荐室友，"我的社区"(My Community) 语言筛选还能帮你找到会说中文或同样语言的人。
- **学校和公司资源**：大学的校外住房平台 (off-campus housing)、校友群、公司内部群，相对更有约束力。
- **朋友介绍**：依然是最安全的方式之一，尽早在朋友圈里问一圈，连"不太可能认识人"的朋友也问问。
- **华人社区渠道**：微信群、小红书、51.ca、约克论坛 (yorkbbs) 上合租信息非常多，更新也快，对刚落地的同学很方便。但这些地方也是假房源、冒充房东、"先转定金"骗局的高发地，后面的核实步骤一步都不能省。
- **综合分类网站**：覆盖面大，但几乎没有筛选，全部要靠自己核实。

### 怎么写一条好的找室友帖子

越具体越好。与其写"人好相处、爱干净"，不如写"护士，每周三个夜班，作息规律，不养宠物，偶尔周末有朋友来访"。把预算范围、目标区域、入住日期放在最前面，能直接过滤掉不合适的人。

在小红书或微信群发帖时，不要把学号、护照、具体门牌号、手机号直接贴出来，有意向的人私聊再说。

## 第三步：初筛候选人

消息多起来以后，要快速、礼貌地筛选。

### 初次沟通检查清单

- [ ] 对方认真回答了你的问题，而不是群发模板
- [ ] 预算和入住时间对得上
- [ ] 愿意视频通话
- [ ] 没有在这个阶段就要钱、要护照照片或银行信息

### 看到这些信号，直接放弃

- 还没看房、没签任何东西，就要你先转"定金""占位费"
- 用各种理由拒绝视频或实地看房，比如"人在国外""钥匙在中介那"
- 租金比同区域同类房源低得离谱
- 不停催你"今天必须定，好多人在抢"
- 说法前后不一致：房子换了、房东换了、理由换了
- 要求用礼品卡、加密货币，或者转账到海外个人账户

这类骗局在多伦多很常见，我们专门写了一篇：[多伦多租房诈骗识别与防范](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 第四步：第一次见面聊什么

建议先视频，再当面，最好直接约在房子里。准备好问题清单，重点聊：钱怎么分、卫生标准、访客和留宿、噪音和作息、是否在家办公、食物共享、宠物。我们整理了一份可以直接用的 [找室友要问的30个问题](/zh/blog/questions-to-ask-a-roommate/)。

几个小技巧：

- **问具体例子，别问标签**："你一般多久洗一次碗？"比"你爱干净吗？"有用得多。
- **主动说自己的小习惯**：你坦诚，对方也更愿意说实话。
- **观察对方怎么处理分歧**：小事上意见不同时，是认真听还是不耐烦？
- **注意人身安全**：第一次去陌生人家里，可以约朋友一起，或者提前告诉家人朋友你的去向。

## 第五步：核实人，也核实房

这一步决定你是顺利入住，还是钱房两空。

### 核实室友本人

- 名字和资料是否一致，有没有前任房东或室友可以做推荐人，而且真的打电话问一下。
- 如果对方说自己是学生或在某公司上班，可以简单查一下学校或职业资料是否吻合。

### 核实房源和出租人

- 实地看房；实在来不了，也要让对方实时视频带你一间一间看，打开窗户看看街景，和房源描述对得上。
- 如果有中介，到安省地产委员会 (RECO) 的官网注册查询 (Registrant Search) 里查一下中介是否注册、有没有处分记录。
- 如果是房东直租，问清楚房子是谁的，对方凭什么有权出租。如果是"二房东"，可以请他出示和房东签的租约。
- 坚持签书面租约。在安省，大多数住宅租赁都必须使用政府的标准租约 (Standard Lease)，房东要在你签字后21天内给你一份副本。

### 了解押金规则

在受《住宅租赁法》保护的大多数租约里，房东最多只能收一个月房租作为租金押金（用来抵最后一个月房租），以及可退还的钥匙押金，不能另外收"损坏押金"。记住一句话：没看过房、没签租约，一分钱都不要转。

## 第六步：签一份室友协议

选好人以后，花半小时写一份室友协议，至少包括：

- 房租怎么分，谁负责交给房东
- 水电网费怎么分、怎么付
- 家务分工和公共用品（洗洁精、卫生纸、垃圾袋谁买）
- 访客和留宿规则
- 安静时间
- 有人想提前搬走怎么办，押金怎么退

具体写法、模板和房间大小不一样时房租怎么分，都在 [安省室友协议怎么写](/zh/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/) 里。

## 第七步：入住之后

- **一起做入住检查**：每个房间拍带日期的照片，留好证据，搬走时退押金会用到。
- **把公共账单管清楚**：用共享表格或记账软件，谁付了什么一目了然。
- **两周后聊一次**：趁小问题还没变成大矛盾，坐下来调整一下规则。
- **建一个小群**：室友之间的事在群里说，比在背后吐槽有效得多。

## 给留学生和新移民的几点提醒

刚来加拿大，没有本地信用记录、没有本地推荐人，这很正常。可以准备录取通知书、在职证明、资金证明，或者国内房东的推荐信，让对方放心。

人在国内就要付款的情况要格外谨慎，很多骗局专门针对"还没落地、没法看房"的同学。条件允许的话，先订两三周的短租，落地后再实地看房、见室友。哪怕多花一点短租费，也比提前转几千加元定金却发现房子根本不存在要好。

另外，文化习惯差异也值得提前聊：比如是否经常在家做饭、是否在家里穿鞋、空调和暖气开到多少度、会不会有家人长期来探亲。这些在国内觉得理所当然的事，在合租里往往最容易产生摩擦。

## 用 ColivEase 找到合拍的室友

ColivEase 就是为这件事设计的：AI 根据作息、预算和生活习惯帮你匹配室友；"我的社区"语言筛选让你更容易遇到说同样语言的人；默认使用卡通头像，双方都同意后才互相展示真实照片；房源经过房东和中介认证，并有 AI 诈骗检测。你还可以和朋友组队申请，或者参与整栋房子按房间分租（组队租），每个房间单独申请。[现在就在 ColivEase 开始找室友](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html)。

## 常见问题

**在多伦多找室友一般要提前多久？**
建议至少提前四到六周开始。如果是八九月开学季，竞争最激烈，最好再提前一些。预算越紧、对地段要求越具体，所需时间通常越长。

**在微信群或小红书上找室友安全吗？**
可以用，但要格外小心。这些渠道信息多、更新快，假房源和冒充房东的情况也不少。一定要视频或当面确认身份、实地看房，签好租约之前不要转任何定金。

**只租一个房间，受安省租客法保护吗？**
多数情况下受保护，但有例外。如果你和房屋业主本人或其特定近亲（配偶、子女、父母等）共用厨房或卫生间，《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 一般不适用。签约前最好向房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 或法律援助诊所确认。

**室友协议有法律效力吗？**
室友协议是室友之间的私人约定，不能代替你和房东签的租约，也约束不了房东。但它能把房租分摊、家务、访客、搬走等规则写清楚，发生纠纷时也是重要的书面证据。

**没有加拿大信用记录怎么找室友和租房？**
这对新移民和留学生很常见。可以提供录取通知书、在职证明、资金证明或以前房东的推荐信。如果被要求预付多个月房租，要知道这通常可以协商，付款前务必确认房源真实、租约已签。

## 参考资料

- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights（安省政府）](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease（安省标准租约指南）](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006（安省法律 e-Laws）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Find out if the Residential Tenancies Act applies（Steps to Justice）](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/1-find-out-if-the-residential-tenancies-act-applies/)
- [RECO Registrant Search（安省地产委员会注册查询）](https://registrantsearch.reco.on.ca/)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board（房东与租客委员会）](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
- [Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre（加拿大反诈骗中心）](https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/)

# International Student Housing in Toronto: 2026 Checklist

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-10-31

International student housing in Toronto, step by step: when to start, residence vs off-campus, documents, remote viewings, the lease, deposits and scams.

International students looking for housing in Toronto should start with their school's housing office, apply for residence as soon as they accept an offer, and begin the off-campus search about one to two months before move-in, when most listings appear. Never send money for a place you haven't verified, make sure you sign Ontario's Standard Lease where it applies, and don't pay more than the deposits Ontario allows.

## Key takeaways

- **Residence deadlines come early.** At U of T, for example, first-year students had to apply through the residence portal by March 31 to keep the residence guarantee for 2026 entry.
- **Off-campus listings appear late.** Many tenants give 60 days' notice, so most units hit the market one to two months ahead.
- **Prepare documents now:** passport, study permit or letter of introduction, proof of enrolment and proof of funds.
- **Verify before you pay.** Live video tours and a trusted local contact beat any promise made over chat.
- **Know the deposit limits:** a last month's rent deposit of up to one month's rent and a refundable key deposit. No damage deposits.
- **Use your school.** Housing offices can help you check listings, leases and red flags for free.

## Your timeline at a glance

| When | What to do |
|---|---|
| As soon as you accept your offer | Check residence options and deadlines; apply if you want to live on campus |
| 3–4 months before arrival | Research neighbourhoods near your campus, set a budget, join official school housing platforms |
| 6–8 weeks before move-in | Search actively, book viewings (in person or live video), line up references and proof of funds |
| 2–4 weeks before move-in | Sign the lease, pay deposits by a traceable method, arrange tenant insurance and utilities |
| Move-in day | Inspect the unit, take dated photos, test locks and smoke alarms, and get keys and receipts |

If you can't lock in a long-term place before you fly, book a short-term stay for your first few weeks. Viewing in person after you land is the single best protection against scams.

## Residence or off-campus?

| | Residence (on campus) | Off-campus rental |
|---|---|---|
| Convenience | Steps from class, often with meal plans | Depends on your commute |
| Paperwork | Applied through your school | Application, lease and deposits with a private landlord |
| Cost | Fixed fees set by the school | Varies widely; rooms average about $1,150–$1,220 a month in Toronto |
| Flexibility | Academic-year terms, house rules | Usually 12-month leases; more independence |
| Social life | Built-in community | You choose your roommates |
| Risk of scams | Very low | Higher; verify everything |

Many international students spend their first year in residence and move off campus afterwards. If residence is full or too expensive, our guide to the [best Toronto neighbourhoods for students](/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/) helps you shortlist areas near your campus.

## Documents to have ready

Keep digital copies in one folder so you can apply quickly:

- **Passport** (share a copy only once the landlord is verified)
- **Study permit**, or your port-of-entry letter of introduction if you haven't arrived yet
- **Letter of acceptance or proof of enrolment**
- **Proof of funds**: recent bank statements, scholarship letters or a sponsor's letter
- **References**: a previous landlord, a professor or an employer, if you have them
- **Guarantor information**, if a landlord asks and you have someone in Canada who can help

You don't need a Social Insurance Number to rent. Service Canada lists renting a property and filling out a rental application among situations where you don't have to provide it. If you have no Canadian credit history yet, that's normal for students: offer proof of funds, your enrolment letter and references instead, and remember that a lack of credit history shouldn't be held against you in Ontario.

## Viewing a place remotely, safely

If you're still abroad:

1. **Ask for a live video tour**, not pre-recorded clips. Ask the person to open closets, run the taps, show the view from the window and walk to the front door so you can see the street.
2. **Confirm who they are.** Ask for their full name and check that they own or manage the unit. A property management company should have a website, office address and phone number you can verify.
3. **Ask a trusted friend in Toronto** to view the unit in person if possible.
4. **Search the address and photos online.** Scammers often copy photos from real listings.
5. **Ask your school's housing office** to look at the listing and lease if anything feels off.

## Signing the Standard Lease

Most residential tenancies in Ontario must use the government's Standard Lease form. It sets out the rent, what's included, deposits and the rules both sides must follow. Read the "additional terms" section carefully, because a term that breaks the Residential Tenancies Act can't be enforced, even if you signed it.

If your landlord doesn't give you the Standard Lease, you can ask for it in writing. If they don't provide it within 21 days, Ontario's rules give you options, including withholding up to one month's rent in some circumstances. Our full guide to the [Ontario Standard Lease](/blog/ontario-standard-lease/) walks through each section.

One important exception: if you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's close family, the Residential Tenancies Act generally doesn't apply, and neither does the Standard Lease. That's common in homestays and some room rentals, so ask before you sign.

## Deposits and payments

In Ontario, a landlord can collect:

- A **rent deposit** of no more than one month's rent, which must be used for your last month
- A **refundable key deposit**

Damage deposits are not allowed. The landlord owes you annual interest on the rent deposit at the rent increase guideline rate (2.1% for 2026). A landlord can't make several months of prepaid rent a condition of renting to you; if you choose to offer it, do so only after verifying the landlord and signing the lease, and get a receipt.

Pay by a traceable method, such as an e-transfer to a verified landlord or a cheque, and keep every receipt and message.

## Scams that target international students

Students are targeted because they often rent from abroad, under time pressure. In June 2026, Toronto police announced an arrest in an alleged rental fraud near Yonge and Finch in which international students paid deposits for apartments they hadn't viewed. Watch for:

- **Too-good-to-be-true rent** in popular areas
- **"I'm overseas, I'll mail you the keys"** stories
- **The same unit rented to several people**, each paying a deposit
- **Fake agents** asking for passport and permit copies before any viewing
- **Pressure to pay today** because "many students are interested"
- **Sublets from someone with no right to sublet**

If you're targeted, contact your bank immediately, report to the Toronto Police Service and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, and tell your school's housing office. Read more in our guide to [Toronto rental scams](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/).

## Use your school's housing office

- **University of Toronto:** the Off-Campus Housing Finder is open to students with a UTORid and includes a roommate finder.
- **Toronto Metropolitan University:** the Off-Campus Housing Office offers appointments and resources for current and incoming students.
- **York University:** off-campus housing services include a listing platform and support for tenant-landlord issues.
- **Colleges** such as Humber, Seneca, Centennial and George Brown have housing or student-life teams who can help.

These services are free, and staff have seen every scam in the book.

## After you move in

A few small steps in your first week can save you a lot of trouble later:

- **Document the unit's condition.** Take dated photos and videos of every room, including any damage, and email them to your landlord so there's a record.
- **Get tenant insurance** if you haven't already. It covers your belongings and your liability if, for example, you accidentally cause a leak.
- **Set up utilities and internet** that aren't included in your rent, and confirm whose name each account is in.
- **Save your landlord's contact details** and the process for repair requests, preferably in writing.
- **Pay rent on time and keep receipts.** A clean rental record here becomes a reference for your next place.

## Find roommates you can trust

ColivEase was designed with students in mind. AI matching pairs you with roommates based on habits, budget and schedule, and the "My Community" filter helps you meet people who share your languages. Profiles start with comic avatars, and real photos are only shown when both people agree. Landlords and agents are verified, and listings go through AI scam checks.

Ready to start your search before you land? Browse verified listings, check commute times to your campus and connect with roommates on [ColivEase](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html).

## FAQ

**When should international students start looking for housing in Toronto?**
Apply for residence as soon as you accept your offer, since deadlines can come early in the year. For off-campus rentals, most units are listed about one to two months before they're available, partly because tenants on monthly leases must give 60 days' notice to move out. Start researching neighbourhoods and budgets earlier, and search actively six to eight weeks before your move.

**Can I rent an apartment in Toronto before I arrive in Canada?**
Yes, but it's riskier. If you sign from abroad, verify the landlord's identity, get a live video tour, ask someone you trust in Toronto to view it in person, and only pay after you've signed a written lease. Many students book a short-term stay for the first few weeks and sign a long-term lease after viewing in person.

**What documents do international students need to rent in Toronto?**
Landlords usually ask for a passport, your study permit or letter of introduction, proof of enrolment, proof of funds such as bank statements, and references if you have them. Some also ask for a guarantor. You don't need to give your Social Insurance Number to rent.

**Is it safe to pay a deposit before seeing a place?**
It's one of the most common ways students lose money. Never pay before you've verified that the person owns or manages the unit and you've seen it in person or on a live video call. Pay by a traceable method and get a receipt.

**Does the Ontario Standard Lease apply if I rent a room?**
Usually yes, if the Residential Tenancies Act applies to your rental. A key exception is when you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's close family; then the Act and the Standard Lease generally don't apply, and you have fewer protections.

**Where can international students get help with housing in Toronto?**
Start with your school's housing office. U of T has an Off-Campus Housing Finder, TMU has an Off-Campus Housing Office, and York has off-campus housing services. Colleges also have housing or student-life staff who can review listings and leases with you.

- [York University: Off-campus housing](https://www.yorku.ca/housing/off-campus-housing/)
- [Government of Ontario: Guide to Ontario's Standard Lease](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Government of Ontario: Renting in Ontario, your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board: Information for new tenants](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Brochures/Information%20for%20New%20Tenants.pdf)
- [IRCC: Study in Canada as an international student](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada.html)
- [Service Canada: When to provide your SIN (code of practice)](https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/esdc-edsc/documents/services/sin/reports/code-of-practice/2.5_when-provide-sin_en.pdf)
- [Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre](https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/)
- [CTV News: Arrest in alleged rental fraud targeting international students in North York (June 2026)](https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/woman-arrested-in-alleged-rental-fraud-targeting-international-students-in-north-york/)

# 多伦多留学生租房全攻略：时间线与避坑清单

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-10-31

多伦多留学生租房完整清单：什么时候开始找、住宿舍还是校外、要准备哪些材料、人在国内怎么安全看房、标准租约和押金规定，以及专门针对留学生的骗局。

多伦多留学生租房，最重要的三件事：**先找学校住房办公室、宿舍要早申请、校外租房在入住前一到两个月集中找**。没有核实过的房子一分钱都不要付；签约尽量使用安省标准租约 (Standard Lease)；押金不要超过安省法律允许的范围。下面按时间顺序，把从拿到录取到搬进新家的每一步都列清楚。

## 先看重点

- **宿舍截止日期很早**：以多伦多大学 (U of T) 为例，2026 年入学的一年级新生要在 3 月 31 日前通过宿舍系统提交申请，才能保留宿舍保证资格。
- **校外房源出得晚**：按月租住的租客搬走要提前 60 天通知房东，所以大部分房源在入住前一到两个月才上市。
- **材料现在就准备**：护照、学签或签证批准信、在读证明、资金证明。
- **先核实、再付款**：实时视频看房、本地朋友帮忙实地看，比任何聊天记录里的承诺都可靠。
- **押金有上限**：最多一个月房租的押金（抵最后一个月）加可退还的钥匙押金，不允许收损坏押金。
- **善用学校资源**：学校住房办公室可以免费帮你看房源、看租约、识别骗局。

## 租房时间线

| 时间 | 要做的事 |
|---|---|
| 接受录取后 | 了解宿舍选项和截止日期，想住校就尽快申请 |
| 入学前 3–4 个月 | 研究学校周边社区、定预算、注册学校官方租房平台 |
| 入住前 6–8 周 | 集中找房，预约看房（实地或实时视频），准备推荐信和资金证明 |
| 入住前 2–4 周 | 签租约，用可追踪的方式付押金，办好租客保险和水电网 |
| 搬家当天 | 检查房屋、拍带日期的照片、测试门锁和烟雾报警器，拿到钥匙和收据 |

如果出发前实在定不下长租，可以先订两三周的短租。**落地后实地看房，是防骗最有效的一招。**

## 住宿舍还是校外租房？

| | 学校宿舍 | 校外租房 |
|---|---|---|
| 便利程度 | 离教室近，常配餐卡 | 取决于通勤 |
| 手续 | 通过学校申请 | 和私人房东签申请、租约、付押金 |
| 费用 | 学校统一定价 | 差别很大，多伦多单间平均约 1,150–1,220 加元/月 |
| 灵活度 | 按学年入住，有宿舍规定 | 一般签 12 个月，更自由 |
| 社交 | 自带社交圈 | 室友自己选 |
| 被骗风险 | 很低 | 较高，样样都要核实 |

很多留学生第一年住宿舍，第二年再搬出去住。如果宿舍满了或太贵，可以先看看 [多伦多留学生住哪里](/zh/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/)，按校区挑社区。

## 需要准备的材料

把电子版放在同一个文件夹里，看到合适的房子可以马上申请：

- **护照**（确认房东真实后再发复印件）；
- **学签**，如果还没入境，可以先提供签证批准信 (letter of introduction)；
- **录取信或在读证明**；
- **资金证明**：近期银行流水、奖学金证明或父母的资助说明；
- **推荐信**：以前的房东、老师或雇主（有的话）；
- **担保人信息**：如果房东要求，并且你在加拿大有人可以帮忙。

租房不需要社会保险号 (SIN)。加拿大服务部把租房、填写租房申请列为不必提供 SIN 的情形。没有加拿大信用记录也很正常，用资金证明、在读证明和推荐信代替即可；在安省，没有信用记录本身不应该被当作扣分项。

## 人在国内，怎么安全"云看房"？

1. **要求实时视频看房**，不要只看对方发来的录像。请对方打开衣柜、开水龙头、拍窗外的景色，再走到门口拍一下街道。
2. **核实对方身份**：问清全名，确认他是业主或物业管理方。正规物业公司会有官网、办公地址和电话，可以自己打过去核实。
3. **请多伦多信得过的朋友**帮忙实地看一次。
4. **用地址和图片搜索一下**，骗子经常盗用真实房源的照片。
5. **拿不准就问学校住房办公室**，请老师帮你看看房源和租约。

## 中文找房渠道：方便，但更要小心

很多同学会在微信群、小红书、51.ca 和约克论坛上找房、找室友。这些渠道沟通方便、更新快，还能找到生活习惯相近的中国室友，但也是假房源、冒充房东、一房多租的重灾区，尤其是每年七八月开学季前。

几个底线：对方不肯视频、只催你转定金的，不要继续；价格明显低于同区域行情的，先打个问号；"学长学姐转租"要确认他是否有权转租、房东是否同意；聊天中途换账号、要求你换平台私聊付款的，都要警惕。

## 签订安省标准租约

安省大多数住宅租赁都必须使用政府的标准租约，上面写明房租、包含哪些费用、押金，以及双方必须遵守的规则。重点看"附加条款" (additional terms)：违反《住宅租赁法》的条款，即使你签了字也无效。

如果房东没给你标准租约，你可以书面要求；房东在 21 天内仍不提供的，安省规定给了你一些选择，在某些情况下可以暂扣最多一个月的房租。详细解读见 [安省标准租约](/zh/blog/ontario-standard-lease/)。

**重要例外**：如果你和房屋业主本人或其近亲共用厨房或卫生间，《住宅租赁法》一般不适用，标准租约也不适用。寄宿家庭 (homestay) 和部分"房东同住"的单间就属于这种情况，签约前一定问清楚。

## 押金和付款

在安省，房东可以收取：

- **租金押金**：不超过一个月房租，只能用来抵最后一个月房租；
- **可退还的钥匙押金**。

损坏押金是不允许的。房东每年要按当年涨租指导线给押金算利息（2026 年为 2.1%）。房东不能把预付几个月房租作为出租条件；如果你自己决定主动预付，也要在核实房东、签好租约之后再付，并拿到收据。

付款用可追踪的方式，比如 e-transfer 给已核实的房东，或支票；所有收据和聊天记录都要保存好。

## 专门针对留学生的骗局

留学生常常人在国外、时间紧，最容易成为目标。2026 年 6 月，多伦多警方通报在 Yonge 和 Finch 附近一宗涉嫌租房诈骗案中逮捕一名嫌疑人，受害者多为没看房就付了定金的国际学生。常见套路包括：

- **热门地段房租低得离谱**；
- **"我在国外，钥匙寄给你"**；
- **同一套房租给好几个人**，每人都交了定金；
- **假中介**还没看房就要护照、学签照片；
- **催你今天就付钱**，说"好多同学在抢"；
- **无权转租的人**把房子"转租"给你。

如果不幸遇到，马上联系银行，向多伦多警察局和加拿大反诈骗中心 (CAFC) 报案，并告诉学校住房办公室。更多防骗要点见 [多伦多租房防骗指南](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 用好学校的住房资源

- **多伦多大学**：Off-Campus Housing Finder 面向持 UTORid 的学生，还有找室友功能。
- **TMU**：Off-Campus Housing Office 为在读和即将入学的学生提供预约咨询和资源。
- **约克大学**：校外住房服务包括房源平台，以及租客和房东纠纷方面的支持。
- **各学院**：Humber、Seneca、Centennial、George Brown 等都有住房或学生事务团队可以求助。

这些服务都是免费的，老师们见过的骗局比你想象的多得多。

## 预算怎么做？

根据多大学生生活办公室 2026 年春季汇总的数据，多伦多一个房间的平均月租大约在 1,150 到 1,220 加元之间，市中心和学校附近通常更贵。除了房租，还要把水电网、租客保险、交通费、买菜和日用品都算进去。刚落地的第一个月开销最大：第一个月房租、最后一个月房租押金、短租过渡、买床垫和锅碗瓢盆，往往加起来是一笔不小的数目，建议提前多准备一些。具体拆解可以参考本站的《多伦多租房多少钱》一文。

另外，留学生在加拿大打工有工时等方面的限制，具体以你的学签条件和移民局 (IRCC) 的最新规定为准。做预算时不要把还没找到的兼职收入算进去，先用确定能到手的钱来规划房租。

## 搬进去之后

入住第一周做好下面几件小事，能省掉以后很多麻烦：

- **记录房屋状况**：给每个房间拍带日期的照片和视频，包括已有的损坏，并通过邮件发给房东留底。
- **买租客保险**：保障你的个人物品；万一你不小心造成漏水等损失，个人责任险也能派上用场。
- **开通水电网**：房租不包含的部分要自己开户，并确认每个账户登记在谁的名下。
- **保存房东联系方式**：问清楚报修流程，最好以书面形式沟通。
- **按时交房租、保留收据**：在这里留下良好的租房记录，下次租房时就是很有分量的推荐。

## 找到靠谱的室友

ColivEase 在设计时就考虑到了留学生的需求：AI 根据生活习惯、预算和作息帮你匹配室友，"My Community"语言筛选能帮你找到说中文的同学；资料默认使用卡通头像，双方都同意后才互相显示真实照片。房东和中介经过认证，房源也会经过 AI 诈骗检测。

还没出发就想开始找房？在 [ColivEase](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html) 浏览已认证房源，查看到学校的通勤时间，提前认识未来的室友。

## 常见问题

**留学生应该提前多久在多伦多找房？**
想住学校宿舍的话，接受录取后尽快申请，截止日期往往在年初。校外租房的房源一般在入住前一到两个月才集中出现，部分原因是按月租住的租客搬走要提前 60 天通知房东。建议提前三四个月开始了解社区和预算，入住前六到八周开始集中找房。

**人还在国内，可以先在多伦多租好房子吗？**
可以，但风险更高。务必核实房东身份、要求实时视频看房，最好请在多伦多信得过的朋友实地看一次，签好书面租约后再付款。很多同学会先订两三周短租，落地实地看房后再签长租。

**留学生租房要准备哪些材料？**
房东通常会要护照、学签或入境前的签证批准信、在读证明或录取信、资金证明（如银行流水），有的话再加推荐信，有些房东还会要求担保人。租房不需要提供社会保险号 (SIN)。

**没看房就先付定金安全吗？**
这是留学生被骗最常见的情形之一。在确认对方确实是房东或物业管理方、并且实地或实时视频看过房之前，不要付任何钱。付款要用可追踪的方式，并保留收据。

**只租一个房间，也适用安省标准租约吗？**
如果你的租赁受《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 管辖，一般都适用。主要例外是你和房屋业主本人或其近亲共用厨房或卫生间，这时 RTA 和标准租约通常都不适用，你能得到的保护也更少。

**留学生租房遇到问题可以找谁？**
先找学校的住房办公室。多大有 Off-Campus Housing Finder，TMU 有 Off-Campus Housing Office，约克大学也有校外住房服务；各学院一般也有住房或学生事务老师，可以帮你看房源和租约。

# Legal Basement Apartment Toronto: What to Check First

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/legal-basement-apartments-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-10-31

Renting a legal basement apartment in Toronto? Check exit windows, smoke and CO alarms, ceiling height and heat, and know the rights you keep if it isn't legal.

A legal basement apartment in Toronto is a second suite that's allowed by the City's zoning and built to meet the Ontario Building Code and Fire Code, usually with a building permit. Before you rent, check for a safe second way out, working smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms, enough ceiling height and reliable heat. Even if a basement unit isn't fully legal, you're still protected by the Residential Tenancies Act (RTA) in most cases.

## Key takeaways

- Toronto zoning allows a **second suite** in most houses, but legal also means **built to code** with permits.
- **Safety first:** a second exit or large enough window, interconnected smoke alarms, and CO alarms where there's fuel-burning equipment.
- Your **RTA rights generally still apply** in a basement unit, legal or not, unless you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner who lives there.
- A landlord **can't lock you out** because the unit isn't legal. Evictions go through the Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB).
- Report fire-safety problems to your landlord in writing, then to **311** if they aren't fixed.

*This is general information, not legal advice. For your situation, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic.*

## What "legal" means for a Toronto basement apartment

There are really two layers:

1. **Zoning: is a second suite allowed here?** The City of Toronto's zoning bylaw allows a secondary suite in most detached houses, semi-detached houses and townhouses across the city.
2. **Building and fire safety: was it built properly?** The suite needs to meet the Ontario Building Code and the Ontario Fire Code. Creating a new suite generally requires a building permit and inspections.

Plenty of basement units in Toronto were finished years ago without permits. They may be on a street where suites are allowed but still miss key safety features. That's why it's worth checking the unit itself, not just asking "is this legal?"

## Basement apartment checklist: what to look at during a viewing

Bring this list and your phone's flashlight. You don't need to be an inspector to spot the big issues.

### Getting out safely

- [ ] Is there a **separate entrance**, or a clear exit that doesn't go through the main unit?
- [ ] If there's only one door, is there a **bedroom window big enough to climb out of**? Building Code standards for exit windows commonly call for an opening of at least 0.35 m², with no side narrower than 380 mm. Ask the landlord to confirm it meets code.
- [ ] Can the window actually be opened from inside without tools? Is it blocked by bars, furniture or a deep window well?
- [ ] Is the path to the exit free of storage and clutter?

### Alarms

- [ ] Is there a **working smoke alarm** in the unit and outside the sleeping area? Ask the landlord to press the test button.
- [ ] In a house with two units, are the smoke alarms **interconnected**, so an alarm upstairs sounds downstairs too?
- [ ] Is there a **carbon monoxide alarm** near the bedrooms? Ontario requires CO alarms in homes with a fuel-burning appliance (such as a gas furnace or water heater), a fireplace or an attached garage.

### Space and comfort

- [ ] **Ceiling height:** can you stand comfortably everywhere? Secondary suites are allowed somewhat lower ceilings than a typical new home, roughly 1.95 m in main areas and a bit less under beams and ducts, but the exact rules depend on when and how the suite was built.
- [ ] **Heat:** does the unit have its own heat source or vents, and do you control the thermostat? Ask how warm it stays in January.
- [ ] **Moisture:** any musty smell, water stains, peeling paint or white crust on the walls? Check under sinks and in corners.
- [ ] **Light and air:** are there windows that open? Is there a bathroom fan that vents outside?
- [ ] **Furnace room:** is it separated from the living space with a door, rather than open to your bedroom?
- [ ] **Electrical:** are there enough outlets, or would you need extension cords everywhere?

### Paperwork and practical details

- [ ] Ask whether the suite was built with a **building permit** and passed inspection.
- [ ] Ask who pays **utilities** and whether your hydro is separate or shared with upstairs.
- [ ] Ask whether **laundry** is shared and when you can use it.
- [ ] Will you get the **Ontario Standard Lease**? Most residential tenancies in Ontario need one. See our guide to the [Ontario standard lease](/blog/ontario-standard-lease/).

### Questions to ask the landlord

1. Was this suite built with a building permit, and did it pass final inspection?
2. When were the smoke and CO alarms last tested or replaced?
3. Has the basement ever flooded or had water come in? What was done about it?
4. How is the unit heated, and is there air conditioning or a dehumidifier in summer?
5. Who lives upstairs, and do we share laundry, the entrance or the backyard?
6. Are utilities included, or split with the upstairs unit? How is the split calculated?

## Legal vs unpermitted: what's different for you?

| Question | Legal, permitted suite | Unpermitted suite |
|---|---|---|
| Does the RTA protect me? | Yes, in most cases | Generally yes, in most cases |
| Can the landlord evict me without the LTB? | No | No |
| Is the landlord responsible for maintenance and repairs? | Yes | Yes |
| Was safety checked by an inspector? | Yes, at the time it was built | Not necessarily |
| Could the City order changes or closure? | Unlikely | Possible, which can disrupt your tenancy |

The biggest practical risk with an unpermitted unit isn't your legal status. It's **safety**, and the chance that the City orders work or the unit stops being rented, forcing you to move on short notice.

## Your rights still apply in a basement unit

If you have your own kitchen and bathroom, the RTA generally covers you in a basement apartment, permitted or not. That means:

- your rent deposit can't be more than one month's rent,
- rent increases follow the provincial rules,
- the landlord must keep the unit in a good state of repair and meet health, safety and maintenance standards,
- the landlord must give proper written notice before entering, except in emergencies, and
- the landlord needs a valid notice and an LTB order to evict you if you don't leave voluntarily.

**One big exception:** if you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner (or the owner's close family) who lives in the house, the RTA may not apply. Read our guide to [living with your landlord in Ontario](/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/).

Also, don't stop paying rent because the unit has problems. Withholding rent can lead to an eviction application against you. Use the proper process instead.

## How to report a problem

1. **Tell your landlord in writing.** Email or text works. Describe the problem, add photos and ask for a repair date.
2. **For smoke or CO alarm problems,** the City of Toronto advises tenants to notify the landlord, and if the landlord doesn't act, to call **311** for a referral to Toronto Fire Services.
3. **For other maintenance or property standards issues** (heat, mould, pests, leaks), you can also contact **311**.
4. **Apply to the LTB.** If repairs aren't done, a tenant can file a maintenance application (Form T6). If the landlord harasses you or locks you out, Form T2 covers tenant rights issues.
5. **Emergencies:** if there's fire, smoke or a CO alarm going off, get out and call **911**.

## Finding a safe basement with ColivEase

Basement units can be a smart, affordable choice in Toronto, especially when you split costs. On ColivEase, listings go through landlord and agent verification plus AI scam checks, and each listing shows whether the host lives in the home. You can run your lease through the AI lease check before signing, and use AI roommate matching to find someone compatible to share a two-bedroom basement with. For a sense of what's fair to pay, see our breakdown of the [cost of renting a room in Toronto](/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/).

## Rent with confidence

A good basement apartment is bright enough, warm enough and, above all, safe to get out of. Use the checklist above at every viewing, ask direct questions and get everything in writing. When you're ready, [browse verified listings on ColivEase](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html) and find a home that's right for you.

## FAQ

**Are basement apartments legal in Toronto?**
Yes, the City of Toronto's zoning allows second suites in most detached houses, semi-detached houses and townhouses. A suite also needs to meet the Ontario Building Code and Fire Code, and creating one generally requires a building permit. A basement can be allowed by zoning but still not be built to code.

**Do I have tenant rights if my basement apartment is illegal?**
In most cases, yes. The Residential Tenancies Act generally applies to a rental unit whether or not the suite was built with permits, unless an exemption applies, such as sharing a kitchen or bathroom with the owner who lives there. Your landlord still needs to follow the LTB process to end your tenancy.

**How do I know if a basement apartment is legal?**
Ask the landlord whether the suite was created with a building permit and passed inspection, and ask to see the paperwork. Also check the basics yourself: a second way out, working interconnected smoke alarms, CO alarms if there's a furnace or other fuel-burning appliance, and adequate heat and ceiling height.

**Who do I call about fire safety problems in my Toronto basement unit?**
Tell your landlord in writing first. If smoke or CO alarms aren't fixed, call 311, which can refer the issue to Toronto Fire Services for inspection. Call 911 if there's smoke, fire or a CO alarm sounding.

**Can my landlord evict me because the basement isn't legal?**
Your landlord can't simply change the locks or tell you to leave. To end a tenancy covered by the RTA, they need a valid notice and, if you don't leave, an order from the Landlord and Tenant Board. Get advice quickly if this happens.

- [City of Toronto: Smoke alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/smoke-alarms/)
- [City of Toronto: Carbon monoxide alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/carbon-monoxide-alarms/)
- [Ontario: Carbon monoxide safety](https://www.ontario.ca/cosafety)

- [Landlord and Tenant Board](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)

# 多伦多地下室租房：合法吗？看房必查清单

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/legal-basement-apartments-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-10-31

多伦多地下室租房便宜，但安全最要紧：层高、逃生窗、烟雾和一氧化碳报警器、暖气怎么查？没有许可的地下室，租客权益还在吗？看房前请收好这份实用清单。

多伦多地下室租房，所谓"合法地下室"，是指市政分区规定允许设立、并且按照安省建筑规范 (Ontario Building Code) 和消防规范 (Fire Code) 建造的附属单元 (second suite)，通常需要建筑许可。看房时最要紧的是：有没有安全的第二出口、烟雾和一氧化碳报警器是否正常、层高和暖气够不够。即使地下室不完全合法，大多数情况下你仍然受住宅租赁法 (RTA) 保护。

对刚落地的留学生和新移民来说，地下室常常是预算内最现实的选择：价格比楼上低、离地铁站和学校近、有时还有独立入口。但地下室的安全问题也最多，下面这份清单建议收藏，看房时逐项对照。

## 要点速览

- 多伦多允许大部分住宅设一个**附属单元**，但"合法"还要**按规范建造**、有许可。
- **安全第一**：第二出口或足够大的逃生窗、联动烟雾报警器、有燃气设备时必须有一氧化碳报警器。
- 地下室无论合不合法，**RTA一般都保护你**；例外是和住在家里的房东共用厨房或卫生间。
- 房东**不能因为地下室不合法就换锁赶人**，必须走房东租客委员会 (LTB) 程序。
- 安全问题先书面通知房东，没有解决就打**311**。

*本文仅为一般信息，不构成法律意见；具体情况请咨询房东租客委员会 (LTB) 或社区法律援助诊所 (community legal clinic)。*

## 多伦多地下室怎样才算"合法"？

其实分两层：

1. **分区 (zoning)：这里允许设附属单元吗？** 多伦多市的分区条例允许全市大部分独立屋、半独立屋和镇屋设一个附属单元。
2. **建筑和消防：是不是按规范建的？** 附属单元需要符合安省建筑规范和消防规范，新建一般需要申请建筑许可 (building permit) 并通过检查。

很多多伦多老房子的地下室是多年前自己装修的，没有许可。它所在的街道也许允许设附属单元，但安全设施可能不达标。所以，与其只问"合不合法"，不如亲自把下面这些项目检查一遍。

## 多伦多地下室看房必查清单

带上这份清单和手机手电筒，不需要专业知识也能发现大问题。

### 逃生出口

- [ ] 有没有**独立入口**，或者不需要经过楼上住户就能出去的出口？
- [ ] 如果只有一扇门，卧室里有没有**能爬出去的窗户**？建筑规范对逃生窗常见的要求是开口面积不小于0.35平方米、任何一边不窄于380毫米，可以请房东确认是否达标。
- [ ] 窗户能不能从里面徒手打开？有没有被防盗栏、家具或很深的窗井挡住？
- [ ] 通往出口的路上有没有堆杂物？

### 报警器

- [ ] 单元内、卧室外面有没有**能正常工作的烟雾报警器**？请房东当场按测试键。
- [ ] 楼上楼下两个单元的烟雾报警器是否**联动**（楼上响，楼下也会响）？
- [ ] 卧室附近有没有**一氧化碳报警器** (CO alarm)？安省规定，家里有燃气炉、燃气热水器等燃料设备、壁炉或连体车库的，必须安装一氧化碳报警器。

### 空间和舒适度

- [ ] **层高**：能不能到处都舒服地站直？附属单元允许的层高比一般新房低一些，主要区域大约1.95米，横梁和风管下方还可以更低，具体要求取决于建造时间和方式。
- [ ] **暖气**：单元有没有独立暖气或出风口？温度能不能自己调？问问房东一月份屋里有多暖。
- [ ] **潮湿**：有没有霉味、水渍、墙皮脱落、墙上白色结晶？看看水槽下面和墙角。
- [ ] **采光通风**：有没有能打开的窗？卫生间的排风扇是否通向室外？
- [ ] **锅炉房**：炉子所在房间有没有门和居住空间隔开？
- [ ] **电路**：插座够不够用？会不会到处拉接线板？

### 文件和生活细节

- [ ] 问清楚这个单元有没有**建筑许可**、是否通过检查。
- [ ] **水电网**谁付？电表是独立的，还是和楼上共用分摊？
- [ ] **洗衣机**是否共用？什么时间可以用？
- [ ] 会不会签**安省标准租约** (Ontario Standard Lease)？安省大多数住宅租赁都需要使用，详见[安省标准租约指南](/zh/blog/ontario-standard-lease/)。

### 看房时可以直接问房东的问题

1. 这个单元有没有建筑许可？最后有没有通过检查？
2. 烟雾报警器和一氧化碳报警器最近一次测试或更换是什么时候？
3. 地下室以前有没有进过水、淹过？后来怎么处理的？
4. 冬天靠什么供暖？夏天有没有空调或除湿机？
5. 楼上住的是谁？洗衣机、入口、后院是否共用？
6. 水电是包在房租里，还是和楼上分摊？怎么算？

### 冬天和雨季要特别留意

多伦多冬天漫长寒冷，地下室贴近地面，保暖和防潮尤其重要。看房最好选在白天，留意光线；如果是夏天看房，记得问冬天的室温和暖气情况。春季融雪和夏季暴雨时，地下室比较容易进水，可以看看地面和墙角有没有水渍、地毯有没有发霉的痕迹，问问房东有没有排水泵 (sump pump)。如果你有很多电子设备或重要证件，不要直接放在地上。买一份租客保险 (tenant insurance)，问清楚是否包含水浸损失，也能多一层保障。

## 地下室租房的优点和缺点

| | 优点 | 缺点 |
|---|---|---|
| 价格 | 通常比同区域的楼上单元便宜 | 便宜得离谱的要警惕安全或诈骗问题 |
| 隐私 | 常有独立入口，不用和房东碰面 | 楼上脚步声、说话声可能比较明显 |
| 位置 | 很多在成熟社区，靠近地铁和学校 | 部分老房子离公共交通较远 |
| 舒适度 | 夏天相对凉快 | 采光较少，冬季和雨季容易潮湿 |
| 安全 | 按规范建造的单元有逃生出口和联动报警器 | 无许可单元未必经过检查 |

总的来说，地下室并不等于"差房子"。只要安全设施到位、房东负责，很多同学和新移民在地下室住得很舒服，还省下不少房租。关键是看房时不怕麻烦，多看、多问、多拍照。

## 合法 vs 无许可地下室：对你有什么不同？

| 问题 | 有许可的合法单元 | 无许可单元 |
|---|---|---|
| 受RTA保护吗？ | 大多数情况受保护 | 一般也受保护 |
| 房东能不经LTB赶人吗？ | 不能 | 不能 |
| 房东要负责维修吗？ | 要 | 要 |
| 安全有没有人检查过？ | 建造时检查过 | 不一定 |
| 市政府会不会要求整改或停用？ | 可能性小 | 有可能，会打乱你的租住计划 |

无许可地下室最大的风险其实不是法律身份，而是**安全**，以及市政府要求整改、单元不能再出租时，你可能要临时搬家。

## 住地下室，你的权利一样在

只要你有独立的厨房和卫生间，无论有没有许可，RTA一般都适用：

- 押金不能超过一个月租金；
- 涨租要遵守省政府的规定；
- 房东必须保持房屋良好维修状态，符合健康、安全和维护标准；
- 除紧急情况外，房东进门前必须提前书面通知；
- 你不愿意搬走时，房东需要合法通知加LTB的命令才能驱逐你。

**重要例外：** 如果你和住在家里的房东（或其近亲）共用厨房或卫生间，RTA可能不适用，详见[和房东同住：安省租房指南](/zh/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/)。

另外，千万不要因为房子有问题就自行停交房租。扣租可能让房东反过来向LTB申请驱逐你，应该走正规流程。

## 入住后，自己也要做好的几件事

- 每个月按一次烟雾报警器和一氧化碳报警器的测试键，听到"滴滴"的低电提示要马上告诉房东；
- 不要拆掉报警器的电池，也不要用东西把报警器罩住，做饭油烟大就开窗、开抽油烟机；
- 逃生窗前不要堆放箱子和家具，保证随时能打开；
- 电暖器远离窗帘和床单，不用的时候关掉；
- 和室友约好着火时在屋外哪里集合。

## 遇到问题，怎么投诉？

1. **书面通知房东。** 邮件或短信都行，写清问题、附上照片，并要求给出维修时间。
2. **烟雾或一氧化碳报警器的问题**：多伦多市建议先通知房东；房东不处理的，打**311**，会转介给多伦多消防局 (Toronto Fire Services)。
3. **暖气、发霉、虫害、漏水等维护问题**：也可以联系**311**。
4. **向LTB申请。** 维修一直不做，租客可以提交T6表格（维护问题）；被骚扰或被锁在门外，可以用T2表格（租客权益问题）。
5. **紧急情况**：着火、冒烟或一氧化碳报警器响，立刻离开并拨打**911**。

## 用ColivEase找安全的地下室

在多伦多，和室友分摊一套两居室地下室，是非常划算的选择。ColivEase上的房源会经过房东和中介认证以及AI防诈检查，每个房源也会标明房东是否住在家里。签约前可以用AI租约检查过一遍条款；AI室友匹配则能帮你按作息、预算和生活习惯找到合拍的室友，还可以用"My Community"语言筛选找到说中文的伙伴。想知道多少钱算合理，可以参考[多伦多租单间要花多少钱](/zh/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/)。

## 安心租好每一间地下室

好的地下室，要够亮、够暖，最重要的是出事时能安全逃出去。每次看房都把上面的清单过一遍，问题直接问，约定写在纸上。准备好了，就[在ColivEase浏览经过认证的房源](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html)，找到真正适合你的家。

## 常见问题

**多伦多的地下室公寓合法吗？**
多伦多市的分区规定 (zoning) 允许大部分独立屋、半独立屋和镇屋设一个附属单元 (second suite)。但合法还要求符合安省建筑规范 (Building Code) 和消防规范 (Fire Code)，新建通常需要建筑许可。分区允许，不代表这套地下室一定按规范建造。

**地下室不合法，我还受租客法保护吗？**
大多数情况下仍受保护。住宅租赁法 (RTA) 一般适用于出租单元，不管它有没有建筑许可；例外是你和住在家里的房东共用厨房或卫生间。房东要终止租约，仍须走LTB的程序。

**怎么判断地下室是不是合法的？**
直接问房东这个单元是否有建筑许可 (building permit)、是否通过检查，并请对方出示文件。同时自己检查：有没有第二个出口、烟雾报警器是否联动、有燃气炉等设备时有没有一氧化碳报警器、暖气和层高是否够。

**地下室报警器坏了房东不修，找谁？**
先书面通知房东。如果烟雾或一氧化碳报警器的问题没有解决，可以打311，市政府会转介给多伦多消防局 (Toronto Fire Services) 检查。有烟、火或一氧化碳报警响起时，立即离开并拨打911。

- [City of Toronto: Smoke alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/smoke-alarms/)
- [City of Toronto: Carbon monoxide alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/carbon-monoxide-alarms/)

# Living With Your Landlord in Ontario: Know the RTA Gap

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-10-31

Living with your landlord in Ontario? If you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner, the RTA may not apply. Learn what changes and how to protect yourself.

If you rent a room in Ontario and must share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner (or the owner's spouse, child or parent) who lives in the same building, the Residential Tenancies Act (RTA) usually does not apply to you. That means no Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB), no standard lease requirement and no RTA rules on notice or deposits. Your protection comes mostly from what you agree to in writing, so a clear room rental agreement matters more than ever.

## Key takeaways

- The RTA exemption in section 5(i) applies when you must share a **kitchen or bathroom** with the owner or certain close family members **who live in the building**.
- If you have your own kitchen and bathroom (for example, a self-contained basement unit), the RTA generally still protects you, even if the owner lives upstairs.
- In an exempt arrangement, the LTB can't hear your dispute. Money claims usually go to Small Claims Court.
- Rules like the one-month deposit cap and the annual rent increase guideline don't automatically apply, so negotiate them into your agreement.
- A written agreement covering notice, deposits, house rules and guests is your best protection.

## When the RTA doesn't apply: the shared kitchen or bathroom test

Section 5(i) of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 exempts living accommodation where the occupant is required to share a bathroom or kitchen with:

- the owner,
- the owner's spouse,
- the owner's child or parent, or
- the spouse's child or parent,

**and** that person lives in the building where the room is.

Both parts matter. Sharing a kitchen with other renters (but not the owner) does not trigger this exemption. And if the owner's family member only drops by, but doesn't live there, the test isn't met.

### Quick comparison

| Your situation | Does the RTA usually apply? | Where disputes go |
|---|---|---|
| Room in a house, owner lives there and you share the kitchen or bathroom | No (s. 5(i) exemption) | Small Claims Court, or negotiation |
| Room in a house, owner's parent lives there and you share the bathroom | No | Small Claims Court, or negotiation |
| Self-contained basement unit, owner lives upstairs, nothing shared | Yes | Landlord and Tenant Board |
| Room in a house shared only with other tenants, owner lives elsewhere | Usually yes | Landlord and Tenant Board |
| You rent from another tenant (a "head tenant") who holds the lease | It depends; get advice | Varies |

Every situation has its own facts. If you're unsure where you fit, the LTB and community legal clinics can help. *This article is general information, not legal advice. For your situation, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic.*

## What changes when you live with the owner

Living with your landlord can be a great setup: often furnished, utilities included, and sometimes cheaper than a full apartment. But you should know what you're giving up.

### Notice to leave

Under the RTA, landlords must use specific LTB notices and can only end a tenancy for reasons the law allows. In an exempt arrangement, those rules don't apply. There's no N12 form, no LTB hearing and no eviction order needed. The owner can generally ask you to leave on whatever notice your agreement sets out, or on "reasonable notice" if your agreement is silent.

That's why a **written notice period** (for example, 30 days for either side) is so important. It gives both of you predictability.

### Deposits

Under the RTA, a landlord can only collect a rent deposit of no more than one month's rent (plus a refundable key deposit), and damage deposits aren't allowed. In an exempt arrangement, a live-in owner can ask for a damage deposit or a different amount. If you pay one:

- get the amount and purpose in writing,
- write down when and how it will be returned,
- list what deductions are allowed (for example, unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear),
- pay by e-transfer or cheque, never cash without a receipt.

For how deposits work under the RTA, see our guide to [rent deposit rules in Ontario](/blog/rent-deposit-rules-ontario/).

### Rent increases

The provincial rent increase guideline and the 12-month rule come from the RTA. If you're exempt, your agreement controls how and when rent can go up. Ask for a clause that says rent stays the same for a set period and that any increase needs written notice.

### Privacy and entry

The RTA's 24-hour written notice before entry doesn't apply. Since you live in the owner's home, shared spaces are shared. But your bedroom is still your space, so put entry rules in writing too (for example, the owner only enters your room with permission or in an emergency).

### Human rights protections are narrower too

The Ontario Human Rights Code has a similar exemption. Under section 21(1), the Code's housing protections don't apply when the occupant must share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's family who live there. In plain terms, a live-in owner has more freedom to choose who they live with. That's another reason to clarify expectations early.

## How to protect yourself with a written agreement

A room rental agreement doesn't need to be complicated. It should be clear, signed by both of you, and each person should keep a copy.

### Checklist: what to include

- [ ] Names of both parties and the full address, including which room is yours
- [ ] Start date, and whether it's month-to-month or a fixed term
- [ ] Monthly rent, the due date and how you'll pay
- [ ] What's included: utilities, internet, laundry, furniture, parking
- [ ] Deposit amount, what it covers and when it comes back
- [ ] Notice period to end the arrangement, for **both** sides
- [ ] Shared spaces you can use (kitchen, living room, fridge and pantry space)
- [ ] House rules: quiet hours, guests and overnight guests, cleaning, smoking, pets
- [ ] When the owner can enter your bedroom
- [ ] How rent increases work, if any
- [ ] How disputes will be handled (for example, a talk first, then written notice)

If you're signing a roommate-style agreement with other renters, our [roommate agreement guide](/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/) has more clauses you can borrow.

### Keep a paper trail

- Take dated photos of your room on move-in day.
- Keep receipts or e-transfer records for every rent and deposit payment.
- Confirm important conversations by text or email ("Just confirming we agreed I'll move out on March 31").

## Before you say yes: questions to ask the owner

Living with someone is personal. Ask these before you commit:

1. Who else lives here, and who will I share the kitchen or bathroom with?
2. Are there cooking times, food storage rules or kitchen limits?
3. What are the expectations around guests, partners and overnight visitors?
4. What happens if either of us wants to end the arrangement?
5. Is the deposit refundable, and what would you deduct for?
6. Is there a written agreement I can review before paying anything?

A good host won't mind these questions. If someone refuses to put anything in writing or pressures you to send money before a viewing, slow down. Those are classic warning signs of a rental scam.

## If something goes wrong

Because the LTB usually can't help in an exempt arrangement, your options look different:

- **Talk first.** Many problems (noise, cleaning, kitchen use) are solved with a direct conversation and a written follow-up.
- **Small Claims Court.** For money disputes, like a deposit that isn't returned or rent you prepaid, Ontario's Small Claims Court handles claims up to $50,000.
- **Police.** If you feel unsafe, or someone is threatening you or holding your belongings, call the police. Call 911 in an emergency.
- **Legal help.** A community legal clinic can tell you whether the RTA really doesn't apply. Sometimes an arrangement that looks exempt isn't (for example, if the owner doesn't actually live there).

## How ColivEase helps

On ColivEase, every listing shows whether the host lives in the home, so you know before you book a viewing whether you might be outside the RTA. Before signing, you can run the agreement through our AI lease check to spot missing notice periods or unclear deposit terms. And if a live-in room isn't for you, our AI roommate matching can pair you with renters who share your habits, budget and schedule so you can rent a whole place together, with full RTA protection.

## Find a room that fits your life

Living with your landlord can work well when everyone knows the rules from day one. Know whether the RTA applies, get the important terms in writing, and keep records. When you're ready to look, [start your search on ColivEase](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html) and filter for homes where the host does or doesn't live on-site.

For a broader overview of what protects most renters, read our guide to [Ontario tenant rights](/blog/ontario-tenant-rights/).

## FAQ

**Does the Residential Tenancies Act apply if I live with my landlord in Ontario?**
Usually not, if you have to share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's spouse, child or parent (or the spouse's child or parent) and that person lives in the same building. This exemption is in section 5(i) of the RTA. If you have your own kitchen and bathroom, the RTA generally still applies even if the owner lives upstairs.

**How much notice does a live-in landlord have to give me in Ontario?**
Because the RTA's notice rules don't apply in an exempt arrangement, there is no LTB notice form or fixed statutory period. Your written agreement and general contract law decide what is fair, which is why it's smart to put a notice period, such as 30 days, in writing before you move in.

**Can I take a live-in landlord to the Landlord and Tenant Board?**
Generally no. If the RTA doesn't apply, the LTB has no jurisdiction over the arrangement. Money disputes, like an unreturned deposit, usually go to Small Claims Court, which handles claims up to $50,000 in Ontario.

**Can a live-in landlord ask for a damage deposit?**
The RTA's limit of one month's rent as a deposit doesn't apply to exempt arrangements, so a live-in owner can ask for a damage deposit. Get the amount, the conditions for keeping any of it, and the return date in writing, and pay in a traceable way.

**Is the arrangement covered if I share a kitchen with the landlord's adult son but the owner lives elsewhere?**
The exemption covers the owner's child if that child lives in the building and you must share the kitchen or bathroom with them. Situations like this can be fact-specific, so contact the LTB or a community legal clinic if you're not sure.

## Sources

- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (section 5 exemptions)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Renting in Ontario: your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
- [Human Rights Code (section 21 exemptions)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90h19)
- [OHRC Policy on human rights and rental housing](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/policy-human-rights-and-rental-housing)

# 和房东同住：安省租房前必须知道的RTA例外

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-10-31

在安省和房东同住、共用厨房或卫生间？住宅租赁法(RTA)可能不保护你。押金、搬走通知期、涨租和纠纷怎么处理，签约前一文看懂，教你写好租房协议。

在安省租单间，如果你需要和住在同一栋房子里的房东（或房东的配偶、子女、父母）共用厨房或卫生间，安省的住宅租赁法 (Residential Tenancies Act, RTA) 通常不适用于你。也就是说，你不能去房东租客委员会 (Landlord and Tenant Board, LTB) 申诉，RTA关于通知期、押金、涨租的规定也不会自动保护你。和房东同住，最重要的保护就是一份写清楚的书面协议。

很多留学生、新移民刚到多伦多时，都会先在"房东家里租一个房间"：家具齐全、包水电网，价格也比整套公寓便宜。这种安排完全可以很舒服，但前提是你知道自己处在什么法律位置。

## 要点速览

- RTA第5(i)条：必须和**住在楼里**的房东或其近亲**共用厨房或卫生间**，就属于豁免。
- 有独立厨卫的地下室单元，即使房东住楼上，一般仍受RTA保护。
- 豁免情况下，LTB管不了；金钱纠纷一般去小额钱债法庭 (Small Claims Court)。
- 押金上限、每年涨租指引等规则不自动适用，要靠协议约定。
- 通知期、押金、访客、厨房使用规则，统统写进书面协议。

## 和房东同住，什么情况下RTA不适用？

RTA第5(i)条的意思是：如果租客**被要求**和以下任何一位共用卫生间或厨房：

- 房东本人（owner）
- 房东的配偶
- 房东的子女或父母
- 配偶的子女或父母

**并且**这个人就住在你租的房间所在的这栋楼里，那么这段租住关系就不受RTA管辖。

两个条件缺一不可。比如你只是和其他租客共用厨房、房东自己住在别处，就不属于这个豁免；房东的父母偶尔过来做饭但不住这里，也不符合条件。

### 常见情况对照表

| 你的情况 | 通常受RTA保护吗？ | 纠纷去哪里解决 |
|---|---|---|
| 房东住在家里，你和房东共用厨房或卫生间 | 不受（5(i)豁免） | 协商或小额钱债法庭 |
| 房东父母住在家里，你和他们共用卫生间 | 不受 | 协商或小额钱债法庭 |
| 独立门户的地下室，厨卫独立，房东住楼上 | 受保护 | LTB |
| 只和其他租客合住，房东住在别处 | 通常受保护 | LTB |
| 你向持有租约的"二房东"（head tenant）租房 | 视情况而定，建议咨询 | 视情况而定 |

每个人的情况都不一样。*本文仅为一般信息，不构成法律意见；具体情况请咨询房东租客委员会 (LTB) 或所在社区的法律援助诊所 (community legal clinic)。*

### 一个简单的自测方法

问自己三个问题：第一，房东本人或其配偶、子女、父母是不是真的住在这栋房子里？第二，我是不是必须和他们共用厨房或卫生间？第三，这种共用是租房条件的一部分，而不是偶尔借用？三个答案都是"是"，你很可能属于豁免情况；只要有一个"不是"，就值得进一步咨询，你可能仍然受RTA保护。

## 不受RTA保护，具体会有什么不同？

### 1. 让你搬走的通知期

受RTA保护的租客，房东必须用LTB规定的表格、按法定理由才能终止租约，还要经过LTB才能拿到驱逐令。和房东同住的豁免情况下，这些都不需要：没有N12表格，没有听证，房东一般可以按你们协议约定的通知期请你搬走；协议没写的，就只能讲"合理通知"(reasonable notice)，具体多久容易扯皮。

所以，**一定要在协议里写明双方都适用的通知期**，比如任何一方提前30天书面通知。

### 2. 押金

RTA下，房东最多只能收不超过一个月租金的租金押金 (rent deposit)，外加可退还的钥匙押金，不能收损坏押金。可是和房东同住时，这些上限不自动适用，房东可以要求损坏押金 (damage deposit)，金额也可能不同。如果要付押金：

- 把金额和用途写进协议；
- 写清楚什么时候、用什么方式退还；
- 列明哪些情况可以扣钱（比如欠租、超出正常磨损的损坏）；
- 用e-transfer或支票付款，付现金一定要收据。

想了解RTA下的押金规则，可以看我们的[安省租房押金规定](/zh/blog/rent-deposit-rules-ontario/)。

### 3. 涨租

安省每年公布的涨租指引 (rent increase guideline)、12个月才能涨一次等规定都来自RTA。豁免情况下，什么时候能涨、涨多少，主要看协议。建议写上"某段时间内租金不变，涨租需提前书面通知"。

### 4. 隐私和进房间

RTA要求房东进入租客单元前提前24小时书面通知，这一条在同住情况下不适用。客厅、厨房本来就是共用的，但你的卧室仍是你的私人空间，建议在协议里约定：房东只有在你同意或紧急情况下才可以进入你的房间。

### 5. 人权法保护也变窄了

《安省人权法》(Ontario Human Rights Code) 第21(1)条也有类似豁免：租客需要和住在家里的房东或其家人共用厨房或卫生间时，人权法中关于住房歧视的保护不适用。简单说，同住房东在挑选"一起生活的人"时有更大的自由。这也是为什么入住前把期待说清楚很重要。

## 签一份靠谱的租房协议：清单

协议不用很复杂，但要清楚、双方签字、各留一份。

- [ ] 双方姓名、完整地址，写明你租的是哪一间
- [ ] 入住日期，按月续租还是固定期限
- [ ] 月租金额、交租日期和付款方式
- [ ] 包含哪些：水电、暖气、网络、洗衣、家具、车位
- [ ] 押金金额、用途和退还时间
- [ ] **双方**结束租住的通知期
- [ ] 可以使用的公共区域（厨房、客厅、冰箱和储物空间）
- [ ] 家规：安静时间、访客和留宿、打扫分工、吸烟、宠物
- [ ] 房东何时可以进入你的卧室
- [ ] 是否涨租、怎么涨
- [ ] 有矛盾时怎么处理（先沟通，再书面通知）

如果你是和其他租客合租，可以参考[安省室友协议指南](/zh/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/)里的条款。

### 留好证据

- 入住当天给房间拍带日期的照片和视频；
- 每次交租、交押金都保留e-transfer记录或收据；
- 重要的口头约定，用短信或邮件再确认一遍。

## 看房时，记得问房东这几个问题

1. 家里还住着谁？我和谁共用厨房、卫生间？
2. 做饭时间、冰箱空间有没有限制？中餐爆炒可以吗？
3. 朋友来访、男女朋友留宿有什么规定？
4. 如果任何一方想结束，提前多久通知？
5. 押金退不退？什么情况会扣？
6. 付款前能不能先看书面协议？

靠谱的房东不会介意这些问题。如果对方拒绝写任何书面文件，或者没看房就催你转账，要提高警惕，这些都是租房诈骗的常见信号。

## 和房东同住的相处之道

法律之外，同住能不能愉快，很大程度上取决于日常相处。很多纠纷其实不是钱的问题，而是生活习惯的差异：

- **厨房使用**：中餐爆炒油烟大，很多本地房东不习惯。可以提前问清楚能不能开大火、要不要开抽油烟机、做完饭多久内清理完。
- **冰箱和储物**：约定好自己的冰箱格子、储物柜，别人的东西不随便用。
- **安静时间**：留学生经常要赶due熬夜，新移民可能要早起通勤，提前说好晚上几点以后保持安静。
- **访客**：朋友来吃饭可以吗？男女朋友能不能留宿、一个月最多几晚？这些最好写进协议。
- **公共区域**：客厅能不能用来学习、开视频会议？洗衣机每周哪几天归你用？
- **沟通方式**：约定一个固定的沟通渠道，比如短信或微信，有事直接说，别憋着。

把这些说在前面，看起来有点"斤斤计较"，其实是对双方都负责。

## 签约前的危险信号

遇到下面这些情况，建议慢下来、多问几句：

- 房东拒绝提供任何书面协议，只肯口头约定；
- 没看房、没视频通话就要求先转押金；
- 押金金额远高于一个月房租，又说不清用途和退还条件；
- 不让你看自己要住的房间，或者说"房间到时候再定"；
- 对你的私人空间没有任何承诺，比如说"我随时可以进你房间"。

## 出了问题怎么办？

- **先沟通。** 噪音、卫生、厨房使用这类问题，大多能当面谈清楚，再发条文字确认。
- **小额钱债法庭。** 押金不退、预付租金要不回来等金钱纠纷，可以去安省小额钱债法庭，目前受理5万加元以内的索赔。
- **报警。** 感到人身不安全、被威胁或物品被扣留，可以报警；紧急情况打911。
- **法律援助。** 社区法律援助诊所可以帮你判断RTA到底适不适用。有些看起来"同住"的情况其实并不符合豁免条件，比如房东根本不住在这里。

## ColivEase怎么帮你

在ColivEase上，每个房源都会标明房东是否住在家里，看房前你就知道这套房可能不受RTA保护。签约前，可以用AI租约检查 (AI lease check) 看看协议里有没有漏掉通知期、押金条款写得不清楚等问题。如果你更想要完整的RTA保护，也可以通过AI室友匹配，按作息、预算和生活习惯找到合拍的室友，一起组队整租。"My Community"语言筛选还能帮你找到会说中文的室友。

## 找到适合你的房间

和房东同住并不是坏选择，关键是第一天就把规则说清楚：先判断RTA是否适用，把重要条款写进协议，并留好记录。准备好开始找房了，就[在ColivEase上开始搜索](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html)，按"房东是否同住"筛选房源。

想全面了解大多数租客享有的权利，请阅读[安省租客权益指南](/zh/blog/ontario-tenant-rights/)。

## 常见问题

**和房东同住，住宅租赁法(RTA)还保护我吗？**
如果你必须和房东本人或其配偶、子女、父母（或配偶的子女、父母）共用厨房或卫生间，而且对方就住在这栋房子里，通常不受RTA保护，这是RTA第5(i)条的豁免。如果你有独立的厨房和卫生间，即使房东住楼上，一般仍受RTA保护。

**同住房东让我搬走，需要提前多久通知？**
豁免情况下没有LTB的通知表格，也没有法定的固定通知期，主要看你们的书面协议和一般合同原则。所以入住前最好在协议里写明双方都要提前例如30天书面通知。

**和同住房东有纠纷，可以去房东租客委员会(LTB)吗？**
一般不行。RTA不适用时，LTB没有管辖权。押金不退等金钱纠纷通常去小额钱债法庭(Small Claims Court)，安省目前受理5万加元以内的索赔。

**同住房东可以收损坏押金(damage deposit)吗？**
可以。RTA规定押金不超过一个月租金、不能收损坏押金，但这些规则在豁免情况下不自动适用。付押金前务必把金额、扣款条件和退还时间写进协议，并用可追踪的方式付款。

## 参考资料

- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006（第5条豁免）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Renting in Ontario: your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
- [Human Rights Code（第21条）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90h19)
- [OHRC Policy on human rights and rental housing](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/policy-human-rights-and-rental-housing)

# Moving to Toronto Checklist: Your Rental Move-In Guide

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/moving-to-toronto-renter-checklist/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-10-31

Moving to Toronto checklist for renters: tenant insurance, Toronto Hydro and Enbridge, internet, move-in photos, elevator booking, address changes and PRESTO.

Moving into a Toronto rental goes smoothly when you handle four things before the keys change hands: tenant insurance, utilities (Toronto Hydro, Enbridge Gas and water, depending on your lease), internet, and building logistics like elevator booking. Then, on move-in day, photograph everything, test the alarms and collect every key and fob. In your first weeks, update your address with Canada Post and the government, and get set up on the TTC with PRESTO or a tap-to-pay card.

## Key takeaways

- **Read your lease first.** The standard lease tells you which utilities are yours.
- **Book early:** internet installation, the condo elevator and movers can fill up, especially around the first of the month.
- **Document the unit** with dated photos and video before you unpack.
- **Update your address:** your driver's licence within 6 days and your health card within 30 days in Ontario.
- **Transit:** tap PRESTO or a credit or debit card on the TTC; fare capping now applies after 47 paid trips in a calendar month.

## Two to four weeks before move-in

### Confirm your lease

- [ ] You have a **signed copy of your lease**. Most residential tenancies in Ontario must use the **Ontario standard lease**. If your landlord didn't use it, you can ask for one in writing. See our guide to the [Ontario standard lease](/blog/ontario-standard-lease/).
- [ ] You know the **landlord's legal name and address** for sending notices.
- [ ] You know your **rent due date and payment method**. Your landlord can't require post-dated cheques or automatic withdrawals, and must give you a rent receipt if you ask.
- [ ] You've paid only what's allowed. Under the Residential Tenancies Act, a rent deposit can't be more than one month's rent, and key deposits must be refundable.

### Get tenant insurance

Tenant insurance (also called renter's or contents insurance) usually covers your belongings, your personal liability, and sometimes extra living costs if you have to leave the unit after a covered event like a fire. It's not required by law, but many landlords make it a lease condition, and the standard lease has a section for it.

- [ ] Get two or three quotes.
- [ ] Ask whether roommates need separate policies (usually yes, if you're not related).
- [ ] Send proof of insurance to your landlord if your lease requires it.

### Set up utilities

Who pays depends on your lease. Here's how it typically works in Toronto:

| Utility | Who usually provides it | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| Electricity | Toronto Hydro, or a sub-metering company in many condos | Is it included in rent? Does the unit have its own meter? |
| Natural gas (heat, hot water, stove) | Enbridge Gas | Is heat included? Who controls the thermostat? |
| Water | City of Toronto, billed to the property owner | Often included, especially in apartments and condos; in houses your lease may ask you to pay a share |
| Water heater rental | A rental company, in some houses | Is the rental fee included, or billed to you? |
| Internet | Your choice of provider | Book installation early; check which providers serve the building |

- [ ] Open accounts for anything in your name, with a start date of your move-in day.
- [ ] If you share with roommates, decide whose name each account goes in and how you'll split bills. Our guide to [splitting rent fairly](/blog/split-rent-fairly/) covers utilities too.

### Book the move

- [ ] **Condo or apartment?** Ask property management about **elevator booking**, move-in hours, any refundable deposit or fee under the building's rules, and loading-dock access.
- [ ] **Get the condo rules.** As a tenant, you'll need to follow them.
- [ ] Book movers or a truck early. Weekends and month-end dates go fast.
- [ ] Check street parking rules for the moving truck, and ask your landlord about a parking spot.

## Move-in day checklist

### Before you unpack: document everything

- [ ] Walk through each room and take **dated photos and video**: walls, floors, windows, appliances, cabinets, bathroom fixtures.
- [ ] Note existing damage in writing and **email it to your landlord** the same day.
- [ ] Run taps, flush toilets, open windows, and test burners, fridge and laundry.
- [ ] Record meter readings if you're paying for hydro or gas.

### Safety check

- [ ] Press the test button on every **smoke alarm** and **carbon monoxide alarm**. If one doesn't work, tell your landlord in writing right away. The City of Toronto says landlords must keep alarms working, and you can call 311 if it isn't fixed.
- [ ] Find the fire exits, electrical panel and water shut-off.
- [ ] Check door and window locks.

### Keys and access

- [ ] Count every key and fob: unit, building, mailbox, garage, storage locker.
- [ ] Get a receipt for any key deposit.
- [ ] Register your name with the concierge or building office if there is one.
- [ ] Ask how to get packages delivered and how to register guests.

## First two weeks: paperwork and settling in

### Change your address

- [ ] **Canada Post Mail Forwarding** sends your mail from your old address to your new one for a fee. Worth it if you're moving within Canada.
- [ ] **ServiceOntario:** update your **driver's licence and vehicle permit within 6 days** and your **health card within 30 days**. Many changes can be done online in one go.
- [ ] **Canada Revenue Agency:** update your address through your CRA account.
- [ ] **Your bank, employer, school and phone provider.**
- [ ] **Immigration:** if you have an application in progress with IRCC, keep your contact details current with them.

### Get around on the TTC

- [ ] Pay with a **PRESTO card**, PRESTO in your mobile wallet, or tap a **credit or debit card**. A two-hour transfer applies automatically when you tap.
- [ ] Need a discounted fare (youth, senior or Fair Pass)? Those need a PRESTO card set to the right fare type. They don't apply to credit or debit taps.
- [ ] Since September 1, 2026, the TTC caps monthly fares: once you've made 47 paid trips in a calendar month with the same payment method, the rest of your TTC trips that month are free. Use one card consistently to benefit.

### Learn your neighbourhood

- [ ] Find your garbage, recycling and green bin collection day (the City of Toronto's TOwaste app helps).
- [ ] Locate the nearest grocery store, pharmacy, walk-in clinic and library branch.
- [ ] Save **311** for city services and non-emergency issues, and **911** for emergencies.
- [ ] Introduce yourself to your neighbours or roommates.

Still choosing where to live? Our guide to the [best Toronto neighbourhoods for students](/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/) compares commute, cost and vibe.

## If something isn't right after you move in

Small problems often show up in the first few weeks: a slow drain, a window that won't lock, a radiator that stays cold. Deal with them early, while the move-in condition is still fresh.

- **Put repair requests in writing.** A short email with photos, the date you noticed the problem and a request for a repair date creates a record you can rely on later.
- **Keep a simple log** of requests, replies and visits from contractors.
- **Know the entry rules.** For tenancies covered by the Residential Tenancies Act, your landlord generally needs to give 24 hours' written notice before coming in, except in emergencies.
- **Don't hold back rent** because of a repair issue. Withholding rent can lead to an eviction application. If repairs aren't done, the Landlord and Tenant Board has a process for that.
- **Heat, pests, mould or leaks** that aren't fixed can also be reported to the City through 311.

For a fuller picture of what your landlord owes you, see the "Renting in Ontario: your rights" page on ontario.ca.

## Moving in with roommates?

A shared move goes better with a quick plan:

- Agree on who buys shared items (toilet paper, cleaning supplies, router) and how you'll split costs.
- Set up a group chat and a shared bills tracker.
- Talk about guests, quiet hours and cleaning in week one, not week six.

On ColivEase, AI roommate matching pairs people by habits, budget and schedule, and the "My Community" language filter helps you meet people who share your languages. Profiles use comic avatars, and real photos are shown only when both people agree. If you're renting a whole home room by room, you can apply per room or as a team. Before you sign, the AI lease check flags unclear terms so you can ask questions first.

## Settle in with confidence

A great move-in is mostly about timing: insurance and utilities before you arrive, photos and alarm checks on day one, and address changes in the first week. Keep this checklist handy, and when you're ready to find your next place or the right roommates, [get started on ColivEase](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html).

## FAQ

**Is tenant insurance mandatory in Ontario?**
No law requires every tenant to have insurance, but your landlord can make it a condition of your lease, and the Ontario standard lease has a section for this. Even when it's optional, tenant insurance can cover your belongings and your liability if you accidentally damage the building or someone gets hurt.

**Do I need to set up Toronto Hydro myself when I rent?**
It depends on your lease. The standard lease says who pays for electricity, heat and water. If you're responsible for electricity and the unit has its own meter, you usually open an account with Toronto Hydro before move-in; in many condos, a sub-metering company handles electricity instead.

**How soon do I need to change my address in Ontario after moving?**
Ontario requires you to update your driver's licence and vehicle permit within 6 days of moving, and your health card within 30 days. You can do many of these changes online through ServiceOntario.

**Can I use a credit card on the TTC instead of PRESTO?**
Yes. You can tap a credit or debit card, including a mobile wallet, or use a PRESTO card. Discounted fares such as youth or senior require a PRESTO card with the right fare type, and since September 1, 2026 the TTC caps fares so you ride free after 47 paid trips in a calendar month using the same payment method.

**Should I do a move-in inspection in Ontario?**
Ontario doesn't require a formal move-in inspection, but it's one of the best ways to protect yourself. Walk through with your landlord if possible, take dated photos and video of every room, and email them to your landlord so there's a shared record.

## Sources

- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Renting in Ontario: your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [ServiceOntario: Change my address](https://www.ontario.ca/page/change-my-address-ontario-services)
- [Canada Post: Mail Forwarding](https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/personal/receiving/manage-mail/mail-forwarding.page)
- [TTC: Fares and passes](https://www.ttc.ca/Fares-and-passes)
- [TTC: Monthly fare capping](https://www.ttc.ca/farecapping)
- [City of Toronto: Smoke alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/smoke-alarms/)

# 多伦多搬家入住清单：从保险水电到PRESTO

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/moving-to-toronto-renter-checklist/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-10-31

刚到多伦多租房入住？这份多伦多搬家入住清单涵盖租客保险、Toronto Hydro和Enbridge开户、网络、入住拍照、公寓电梯预约、改地址和PRESTO。

在多伦多租房入住，想要顺利，关键是在拿钥匙之前搞定四件事：租客保险 (tenant insurance)、水电燃气（Toronto Hydro、Enbridge Gas和水费，看租约由谁负责）、网络，以及公寓电梯预约等搬家安排。入住当天，先拍照留证、测试报警器、点清所有钥匙和门禁卡；入住后的头一两周，再去Canada Post和政府部门更新地址，办好PRESTO或者直接刷卡坐TTC。

刚落地的留学生和新移民，常常一边倒时差一边搬家，很容易漏掉细节。这份多伦多搬家入住清单按时间顺序排好，照着打勾就行。

## 要点速览

- **先读租约**：标准租约会写明哪些水电费归你付。
- **尽早预约**：网络安装、公寓电梯、搬家公司在月初月底特别抢手。
- **入住先拍照**：拆箱之前，用带日期的照片和视频记录房屋状况。
- **及时改地址**：安省驾照6天内、健康卡30天内要更新。
- **交通**：TTC可以刷PRESTO或信用卡、借记卡；同一支付方式一个月付费满47次后当月免费。

## 入住前2–4周

### 确认租约

- [ ] 手上有一份**签好的租约**。安省大多数住宅租赁都必须使用**安省标准租约** (Ontario Standard Lease)；房东没用的话，你可以书面要求，详见[安省标准租约指南](/zh/blog/ontario-standard-lease/)。
- [ ] 知道**房东的法定姓名和送达地址**，以后发通知要用。
- [ ] 清楚**交租日期和付款方式**。房东不能强制要求远期支票或自动扣款；你要求时，房东必须提供租金收据。
- [ ] 只付了法律允许的款项：根据住宅租赁法 (RTA)，押金不能超过一个月租金，钥匙押金必须可退还。

### 买租客保险

租客保险通常保障你的个人物品、个人责任，有时还包括因火灾等受保事件无法居住时的额外住宿费用。法律并不强制，但很多房东会写进租约，标准租约里也有专门条款。

- [ ] 比较两三家报价。
- [ ] 问清楚室友是否需要各自投保（没有亲属关系的通常要分开买）。
- [ ] 如果租约要求，把保单证明发给房东。

### 开通水电燃气

谁来付，以租约为准。多伦多一般是这样：

| 项目 | 通常由谁提供 | 要确认什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 电 | Toronto Hydro，很多公寓由分表公司负责 | 是否包在房租里？有没有独立电表？ |
| 天然气（暖气、热水、炉灶） | Enbridge Gas | 是否包暖气？温控器谁来调？ |
| 水 | 多伦多市政府，账单寄给业主 | 公寓通常包含；租独立屋时租约可能要求你分摊 |
| 热水器租赁 | 部分独立屋向租赁公司租用 | 租金是否包含，还是单独收？ |
| 网络 | 自选运营商 | 尽早预约安装，问清楼里能用哪几家 |

- [ ] 需要你名下的账户，开户日期设为入住当天。
- [ ] 和室友合租的话，提前商量每个账户挂谁的名字、账单怎么分。可参考[合租如何公平分摊房租](/zh/blog/split-rent-fairly/)。

### 安排搬家

- [ ] **住公寓 (condo/apartment)？** 联系物业预约**搬家电梯** (elevator booking)，问清搬家时段、是否要交可退押金或按楼规收费、卸货区怎么用。
- [ ] **拿一份公寓规定**，租客同样要遵守。
- [ ] 尽早订搬家公司或租车，周末和月底最难约。
- [ ] 查清楚街边停车规定，问房东有没有车位。

### 拿钥匙前和房东确认的事

- [ ] 入住当天几点拿钥匙？房东本人到场，还是把钥匙放在密码盒里？
- [ ] 房间会不会提前打扫干净？墙面需要重新粉刷的，是否已经完成？
- [ ] 家具、电器有哪些是房东的？清单最好写在租约附件里。
- [ ] 垃圾和回收桶放在哪里？收运日由谁把桶推到路边？
- [ ] 有没有前任租客留下的东西？可以扔吗？
- [ ] 紧急维修找谁？晚上和周末打哪个电话？

### 第一周生活采购清单

刚搬进来，最好提前列好清单，避免来回跑：

- **卫浴**：卫生纸、浴帘、毛巾、洗手液、马桶刷；
- **厨房**：锅、碗筷、砧板、洗洁精、垃圾袋、保鲜盒；
- **卧室**：床垫保护套、枕头、被子、衣架、台灯；
- **清洁**：吸尘器或扫把、拖把、抹布、多用途清洁剂；
- **其他**：插线板、急救包、手电筒、一个小工具箱。

和室友合租的话，可以把公共用品分工采购，买完在群里记账，月底一起结算。

## 入住当天清单

### 拆箱之前，先拍照

- [ ] 每个房间拍**带日期的照片和视频**：墙面、地板、窗户、电器、柜子、卫浴。
- [ ] 把已有的损坏写下来，**当天发邮件给房东**留底。
- [ ] 开水龙头、冲马桶、开关窗户，试试炉灶、冰箱和洗衣机。
- [ ] 如果电费或燃气费归你付，记下电表、气表读数。

### 安全检查

- [ ] 按一下每个**烟雾报警器**和**一氧化碳报警器**的测试键。不响就立即书面通知房东。多伦多市规定房东必须保持报警器正常工作，房东不修可以打311。
- [ ] 找到消防出口、电闸箱和总水阀的位置。
- [ ] 检查门窗锁是否完好。

### 钥匙和门禁

- [ ] 点清所有钥匙和门禁卡 (fob)：房门、大楼、信箱、车库、储物间。
- [ ] 交了钥匙押金的，要一张收据。
- [ ] 有前台 (concierge) 的楼，去登记你的名字。
- [ ] 问清楚快递怎么收、访客怎么登记。

## 入住后头两周：手续和适应

### 更新地址

- [ ] **Canada Post邮件转寄** (Mail Forwarding)：付费把旧地址的信件转到新地址，在加拿大境内搬家很实用。
- [ ] **ServiceOntario**：**驾照和车辆登记6天内**、**健康卡30天内**更新地址，很多可以在网上一次办好。
- [ ] **加拿大税务局 (CRA)**：在CRA个人账户里更新地址。
- [ ] **银行、雇主、学校、手机运营商**。
- [ ] **移民局**：如果你在IRCC有正在处理的申请，记得同步更新联系方式。

### 坐TTC出行

- [ ] 可以用**PRESTO卡**、手机钱包里的PRESTO，或者直接刷**信用卡、借记卡**。刷卡后自动享受两小时换乘。
- [ ] 需要优惠票价（青少年、长者或Fair Pass）？要用设置好对应票种的PRESTO卡，刷信用卡、借记卡不享受优惠。
- [ ] 从2026年9月1日起，TTC实行月度封顶：同一支付方式在一个自然月内付费乘坐满47次，当月剩下的TTC乘车免费。所以最好固定用同一张卡。

### 熟悉社区

- [ ] 查好垃圾、回收和绿桶 (green bin) 的收运日，可以用多伦多市的TOwaste应用。
- [ ] 找到附近的超市、药房、免预约诊所 (walk-in clinic) 和图书馆。
- [ ] 记住**311**（市政服务和非紧急问题）和**911**（紧急情况）。
- [ ] 和邻居、室友打个招呼。

还在纠结住哪一区？可以看[多伦多最适合学生的社区](/zh/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/)，对比通勤、房租和生活氛围。

## 第一个月容易忽略的开销

搬家那个月，花钱的地方往往比想象的多。提前留出一笔预算，心里更有底：

- 搬家公司或租车、停车费用；
- 公寓搬家可能涉及的电梯押金或费用（按各楼规定）；
- 网络安装或设备费用；
- 租客保险的首期保费；
- 基本家具、厨具和清洁用品；
- 邮件转寄服务费用。

具体金额因人而异，可以向物业、服务商和保险公司询价后再做预算。

## 入住后发现问题怎么办？

入住头几周，小问题往往会陆续冒出来：下水慢、窗户锁不上、暖气片不热……趁入住记录还新鲜，尽早处理：

- **维修请求用书面形式**：发一封简短的邮件，附上照片，写明发现问题的日期，请房东给出维修时间。
- **简单记个日志**：什么时候报修、房东怎么回复、维修工什么时候来。
- **了解进门规定**：受住宅租赁法 (RTA) 保护的租约，除紧急情况外，房东进门一般要提前24小时书面通知。
- **不要自行扣房租**：因为维修问题扣租，可能让房东向LTB申请驱逐你。维修迟迟不做，可以走房东租客委员会 (LTB) 的正规流程。
- **暖气不足、虫害、发霉、漏水**一直没解决，也可以打311向市政府反映。

## 刚落地的新移民和留学生，别忘了这些

搬家之外，刚到多伦多还有几件事最好在第一个月内完成：

- **社会保险号 (SIN)**：工作需要SIN，可以向Service Canada申请。
- **银行账户**：开户后交房租、e-transfer都方便很多，也能慢慢建立本地信用记录。
- **手机号码**：本地号码方便房东、物业和学校联系你。
- **医疗保险**：符合条件的新移民可以申请安省健康保险 (OHIP)；很多安省大学会为国际学生统一安排UHIP，具体请向学校确认。
- **紧急联系人**：在学校或公司登记新地址和紧急联系人。

## 和室友一起搬进来？

合租搬家，提前定个小计划会轻松很多：

- 商量好公共用品（卫生纸、清洁用品、路由器）谁买、怎么分摊；
- 建一个群聊和共享账单表；
- 第一周就聊清楚访客、安静时间和打扫分工，别等到第六周才吵架。

在ColivEase上，AI室友匹配会根据作息、预算和生活习惯推荐室友；"My Community"语言筛选能帮你找到说中文的伙伴。个人资料用漫画头像，只有双方都同意时才会显示真实照片。组队租一整套房时，可以按房间申请，也可以以团队名义一起申请；签约前，AI租约检查会标出不清楚的条款，方便你先问清楚。

## 安心开始多伦多新生活

顺利入住，说到底就是把握好时间：到达前搞定保险和水电，入住当天拍照、测报警器，第一周更新地址。把这份清单存好；准备找下一个家或合拍的室友时，[来ColivEase开始吧](https://www.colivease.ca/app.html)。

## 常见问题

**在安省租房必须买租客保险吗？**
法律没有规定每个租客都必须买，但房东可以把它写进租约作为条件，安省标准租约里也有专门的租客保险条款。即使不是强制，租客保险 (tenant insurance) 通常能保障你的个人物品，以及意外损坏楼宇或他人受伤时的责任。

**租房要自己开Toronto Hydro账户吗？**
看租约。标准租约会写明电、暖气、水由谁负责。如果电费由你付、而且单元有独立电表，通常要在入住前向Toronto Hydro开户；很多公寓 (condo) 则由分表公司 (sub-metering company) 负责电费。

**搬家后多久要在安省改地址？**
安省要求在搬家后6天内更新驾照和车辆登记的地址，30天内更新健康卡 (health card) 地址。很多变更都可以通过ServiceOntario在网上一次办好。

**坐TTC可以直接刷信用卡吗？**
可以。你可以刷信用卡、借记卡（包括手机钱包），也可以用PRESTO卡。青少年、长者等优惠票价需要设置好票种的PRESTO卡；从2026年9月1日起，同一支付方式在一个自然月内付费乘坐满47次后，当月其余TTC乘车免费。

**入住时需要做验房吗？**
安省没有强制规定，但这是保护自己最有效的方法之一。最好和房东一起检查，每个房间都拍带日期的照片和视频，并当天发邮件给房东留底。

## 参考资料

- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Renting in Ontario: your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [ServiceOntario: Change my address](https://www.ontario.ca/page/change-my-address-ontario-services)
- [Canada Post: Mail Forwarding](https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/personal/receiving/manage-mail/mail-forwarding.page)
- [TTC: Fares and passes](https://www.ttc.ca/Fares-and-passes)
- [TTC: Monthly fare capping](https://www.ttc.ca/farecapping)
- [City of Toronto: Smoke alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/smoke-alarms/)
